svg.aria-label: How to write ഏഴ് ൭: 4 parts, ഏ, ഴ, ്, ൭, one after another
svg.title: Writing ഏഴ് ൭
svg.desc: 4 parts written one after another: ഏ, ഴ, ്, ൭ (malayalam). The parts are in the order the hand writes them, which is not always the order they are typed: a vowel sign written to the left of its consonant comes before it. Each vowel sign is drawn on its own, without the consonant it attaches to. Each part has its own group of frames; frame N of a group shows movements 1 to N of that part, the movement being added drawn in ink over the finished part, whose outline is read from _fonts/NotoSansMalayalam-Static.ttf. Each part is drawn at its own scale from its own cited stroke order, so the strip does not show how large the parts are next to each other, how far apart they sit, or any join between them. Stroke order: ഏ: Rodney F. Moag, Malayalam: A University Course and Reference Grammar (University of Texas at Austin South Asia Institute and COERLL, updated April 2018; CC BY-NC-SA 4.0), Table II 'How to Write Word-Initial Vowel Symbols', p. xviii: movements 1-7 for ഏ, written by hand by Thomas Joseph <https://github.com/matjic/malayalam/blob/7141acd2f310bc8928822a7aec61d1149efa6fa3/docs/assets/images/front-writing-028.jpg>; ഴ: Sriveenkat, Ml ഴ order.gif, Malayalam letter LLLA stroke-order animation, 00:03.0–00:07.4 (Wikimedia Commons, 1 July 2023) <https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Ml_%E0%B4%B4_order.gif>; ്: Sachin Nandakumar, Jayasree: Malayalam handwriting, animated stroke by stroke (github.com/sachn1/jayasree, commit e0c9d57, October 2026), js/src/stroke-data.raw.json: the hand-recorded centre-line stroke for ്, drawn alone; "Jayasree" by Sachin Nandakumar, CC BY 4.0 <https://github.com/sachn1/jayasree/blob/e0c9d57dd32031c948da4d5f8432aae3e22c5bba/js/src/stroke-data.raw.json>; ൭: Sachin Nandakumar, Jayasree: Malayalam handwriting, animated stroke by stroke (github.com/sachn1/jayasree, commit e0c9d57, October 2026), js/src/stroke-data.raw.json: the hand-recorded centre-line stroke for ൭; "Jayasree" by Sachin Nandakumar, CC BY 4.0 <https://github.com/sachn1/jayasree/blob/e0c9d57dd32031c948da4d5f8432aae3e22c5bba/js/src/stroke-data.raw.json>. Source notes on variation: ഏ: Moag's Table II (p. xviii) starts at the foot of the small left arch and climbs clockwise over it to the bar (1), draws the bar to the right (2), climbs the stem (3), runs back down it (4), climbs clockwise over the big arch (5), comes down its right side to the middle (6) and rounds the lower bowl to finish at the bottom right (7). Moag's book is CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, so only these facts (order, start, direction and end) are cited; no drawing is copied. The page is read from the scan in Mathew Jacob's digital edition (github.com/matjic/malayalam, commit 7141acd), which notes that the numbers mark drawing movements that can belong to one continuous stroke, not pen lifts. The grahyam online-handwriting samples (github.com/bluebottlewize/grahyam, no licence, cited as counts only) keep no pen-up marker, but none of the 6 unique samples jumps between consecutive points the way a lift would; they most often start at the middle left (4 of 6) and end at the middle right (3 of 6). SPACE Kerala's Thooval (GPL-3.0, facts only) starts its EE.png at the lower left and ends it at the lower right. Its shape, start and end match Moag's ഏ, which settles that Thooval's EE.png is this letter. Only six grahyam samples exist, so the lift count rests on few recordings: confidence is medium. The path is fitted to the bundled Noto Sans Malayalam outline rather than to Moag's drawing; in that outline the stem runs on below the line and round into the big arch, so the run back down the stem follows it there. ഴ: The 47-frame Gayathri-font animation writes ഴ in one uninterrupted run: left entry arch, clockwise right loop, then the descending inner return and lower hook. This is one attested pedagogical order fitted to the bundled Noto Sans Malayalam outline. ്: Jayasree records the candrakkala drawn alone as one stroke: it starts at the left tip, dips round the bottom of the cup and rises to the right tip (start upper left, end upper right). This is the sign's own ductus only; where it goes against its carrier stays the compositionSource's claim, and no written order against a carrier is claimed. Jayasree keeps one recorded gesture per pen-down stroke, so one stroke means the recorder did not lift. Only these facts (stroke count, start, order, direction and end) are taken; no recorded coordinate is copied. The stroke data is licensed CC BY 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/) as "Jayasree" by Sachin Nandakumar, https://github.com/sachn1/jayasree; this record adapts it, and the pen path is fitted to the bundled Noto Sans Malayalam outline rather than to the recording, which was drawn over the Manjari typeface. One recorder, so confidence is medium. ൭: Jayasree records ൭ as one stroke: from the inner end of the small loop, clockwise round it, up the left side and over the top, then down the right and round below the line to the left (start at the inner loop, end below the line at the left). Noto joins the loop's inner end to the outer stroke, so the path starts at that join. Jayasree keeps one recorded gesture per pen-down stroke, so one stroke means the recorder did not lift. Only these facts (stroke count, start, order, direction and end) are taken; no recorded coordinate is copied. The stroke data is licensed CC BY 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/) as "Jayasree" by Sachin Nandakumar, https://github.com/sachn1/jayasree; this record adapts it, and the pen path is fitted to the bundled Noto Sans Malayalam outline rather than to the recording, which was drawn over the Manjari typeface. One recorder, so confidence is medium.
svg.text: How it is written — 4 parts, one after another
Part 1 of 4 — one unbroken stroke · 7 movements
Part 2 of 4 — one unbroken stroke · 3 movements
Part 3 of 4 — one unbroken stroke · 2 movements
Part 4 of 4 — one unbroken stroke · 3 movements
Part 1: stroke order after Rodney F. Moag, Malayalam: A University Course and Reference Grammar (University of Texas at Austin South Asia Institute and COERLL, updated April 2018; CC
BY-NC-SA 4.0), Table II 'How to Write Word-Initial Vowel Symbols', p. xviii: movements 1-7 for ഏ, written by hand by Thomas Joseph
Part 2: stroke order after Sriveenkat, Ml ഴ order.gif, Malayalam letter LLLA stroke-order animation, 00:03.0–00:07.4 (Wikimedia Commons, 1 July 2023)
Part 3: stroke order after Sachin Nandakumar, Jayasree: Malayalam handwriting, animated stroke by stroke (github.com/sachn1/jayasree, commit e0c9d57, October 2026),
js/src/stroke-data.raw.json: the hand-recorded centre-line stroke for ്, drawn alone; "Jayasree" by Sachin Nandakumar, CC BY 4.0
Part 4: stroke order after Sachin Nandakumar, Jayasree: Malayalam handwriting, animated stroke by stroke (github.com/sachn1/jayasree, commit e0c9d57, October 2026),
js/src/stroke-data.raw.json: the hand-recorded centre-line stroke for ൭; "Jayasree" by Sachin Nandakumar, CC BY 4.0
This order is attested, not standardised; the source records where it varies.
